answerGuidance.attribution: Every care answer says it came from your clinician and when it was recorded.
answerGuidance.plainWords: Speak the clinician's recorded words rather than a summary of them.
answerGuidance.rule: One item out loud, then offer the rest on screen. Long lists go on the card, never into speech.

ambiguousPerson.handling: When more than one person could be meant, ask who and then continue; the server returns a short question to speak.

childSafety.handling: CareLoop keeps adult care plans. A note about a child is refused with a plain explanation and nothing is stored.

crisis.handling: Checked before anything else, before storage and before any plan answer. If the caller or the person they care for sounds in danger, the assistant reads the emergency redirect, saves nothing and does not continue the plan. No intent is allowed to go past that redirect.
crisis.spokenWords: If anyone is in danger right now, please call your local emergency number. In India you can call 112, or the Tele-MANAS mental-health helpline 14416 (toll-free, 24x7). I have not saved this as a care item.

doseFree.mechanism: every outbound field is masked, then checked again; a residual amount is an incident that is counted, not a retry
doseFree.statement: Nothing spoken on this surface may carry a medicine amount. Amounts are replaced with 'your prescribed amount' before an answer is spoken, and the full record is only on the household companion page.

neverAsk: how much of a medicine to take
which medicine to buy, stop or swap
a password, family PIN or household code out loud

nothingInvented.statement: The assistant never suggests, changes, stops or explains the reason for an instruction. It repeats what was recorded, and when it has no recording it says so.
nothingInvented.unsureIsFlagged: anything unclear is returned flagged for the clinician instead of smoothed over

promptInjection.handling: Text that reads like instructions for a system rather than care for a person is refused on the voice surface.

roleDenied.handling: A household role that can't act by voice says so and points at the companion page.

speakerScope.handling: What may be read out depends on who the household is answering. The linked household stores which member hears whose plan and whether an instruction still waiting on the clinician may be spoken to them; a question outside that boundary is refused with one plain sentence that the service itself returns, and the refusal is recorded in that household's own ledger. A household that declares no boundary is answered exactly as before.

unknownItem.handling: An item that is no longer on screen is not guessed at; the plan is asked for again.

unlinked.handling: Anything about a real plan needs the household linked first.
unlinked.spokenWords: Link your CareLoop household account to ask about a care plan.

intentsNotOnThisSurface.reason: no voice intent maps onto it: it is only meaningful where the caregiver can see the whole record on the household companion page

answerGuidance.say: Name the person, say the most immediate item in the clinician's own words, then say how many more there are and offer them on screen.

intents.name: WhatsMyPlanIntent
samples: what did the clinician say for {Person}
what has {Person} still got to do
what was I told to do for {Person}

answerGuidance.say: Give the earliest part of the day with its first item, then say how many other times of day have something left.

intents.name: TodaysPlanIntent
samples: what is the plan for today

answerGuidance.say: Say it is recorded, then say how much is still pending.

intents.name: MarkDoneIntent
samples: the {ItemPosition} thing has been dealt with for {Person}

answerGuidance.say: Read back the clinician's own recorded words for that item and the date they were recorded. Do not supply a reason the recording does not contain: if it does not say why, say that it does not say.

intents.name: ExplainInstructionIntent
samples: why did the clinician say that
what were the exact words for the {ItemPosition} item

answerGuidance.say: Repeat the sentence back exactly as stored and say it now travels with the plan.
Say the names the household plans cover.

intents.name: ListPeopleIntent
samples: who do you have plans for
list the people in the plan
whose plan are you looking after

answerGuidance.say: Give the counts of new, stopped and changed items and the visit they were compared with.

intents.name: WhatChangedIntent
samples: what changed since the last visit
what is new since the last appointment
did anything stop since last time
compare this with the previous visit for {Person}

answerGuidance.say: Say how much of today is done and how much is still pending, in one sentence.

intents.name: DailyDigestIntent
samples: how much of the plan is done

answerGuidance.say: Read out the items still waiting on the clinician, and say they are only questions to ask.

intents.name: PrepareVisitQuestionsIntent
samples: what should I ask at the next visit
prepare questions for the next appointment
what do I need to check with the clinician for {Person}
make me a list for the next visit

answerGuidance.say: Read the item back and ask for a clear yes before anything goes. Never remove on the first request.

intents.name: RemoveInstructionIntent
samples: remove the {ItemPosition} one from the plan
that instruction is wrong, remove it

answerGuidance.say: Say what CareLoop can help with in one or two sentences, and that it only repeats what a clinician recorded.

Say which way the delivery changed, using the line the artifact names for it, then speak again the answer this customer already had. Never say anything about the plan that the held answer did not already say.

Say that the device will answer as that household member for the rest of this session and that what may be read out is bounded by what the household lets that member hear. Name no item, no amount and no flag from any plan.

languageModel.modelDescription: Voice surface for one household's recorded adult care plan. Dose-free by design: no intent collects or returns a medicine amount, and nothing here suggests a medicine, a change or a conclusion.

types.name: CareLoopPerson
types.note: Who the plan is about, said the way families say it. Resolved against the household's own people; an unclear match comes back as a question, never a guess.

types.name: CareLoopItemPosition
types.note: Which item from the plan just read out, by its place in the list. Only places the server resolves are offered, so no item identifier is ever spoken or collected.
types.resolution: ordinal words the server can resolve

types.name: CareLoopPlanSection
types.note: A part of the plan. The value is what a family says and the id is the kind the server's own contract names, so a synonym can never be sent as an argument the tool would reject.

types.name: CareLoopNoteText
types.note: The caller's own words for something the family was told verbally. CareLoop stores them as spoken and adds nothing of its own.

types.name: CareLoopDeliveryStyle
types.note: How an answer is spoken, never what it says. Each value is a style id that `presentation.delivery.styles` maps to a rate, a volume and a word ceiling, so the device reads the numbers from this artifact instead of hard-coding them, and a tighter answer is still the same sentence cut to length rather than a new sentence.

notes: One intent per voice-allowed tool, plus device-local intents that call nothing at all. A tool name appears only inside routing and is never spoken.

Each intent declares its slots (name, type, required) for dialog delegation, and routing.slotArguments maps a collected slot onto the server's own argument name. A slot with no mapping is collected for speaking and confirmation only and is never sent.
Brand terms are the five policy_guard._BANNED_KEYWORDS look for. They do not appear in the developer's own copy: the surfaces are called 'your assistant' and 'the companion page'.

presentation.note: How an answer is spoken is an accessibility setting, not a care decision. The styles below are the whole vocabulary a customer can ask for, and each one carries the rate, the volume and the word ceiling the device applies — in SSML, to the sentence the server already returned. A shorter answer is the same sentence cut to length, never a new sentence, because this repo does not write health text. The intent that collects a style routes to no tool, so asking to be understood better cannot change a plan.

proactive.note: One device-initiated turn, for the thing a caregiver cannot remember to ask about: the plan they had just looked at. The skill asks the device to start a connection and the device resumes its own session when the interval declared here has passed — the Connections resume path, with a connection name that is ours and is labelled as such, because a simulated device has no platform routine to read. What the resumed session says is the same read-only tool call the customer could have made, and the dose gate is in front of it like every other voice answer. The device writes nothing on this path.

promptCatalog.note: Prompts are plain sentences for speaking. They never name an internal field, a code, an identifier or a technical format, and every one fits inside maxSpokenSeconds.

body: CareLoop is ready. Ask what is next for someone, why an instruction was given, or say what you want remembered.
I only repeat what your clinician recorded for this household. I can tell you what is next, why something was said, what changed, and what is still to do.
I didn't catch that. You can ask what is next for someone, or what changed since the last visit.
Who should I ask about? Say the name or the relation, like my mother.
Which one on the list? Say the first, the second, the third, the fourth or the fifth.
What should I remember? Say the sentence in your own words and I keep it exactly as you say it.
Link your CareLoop household account to ask about a care plan.
I don't have a recording about that. Ask for the plan again, then refer to an item by its place, like the second one.
Your household role can't do that by voice. You can do it on the CareLoop companion page.
Just to check. Should I really remove the {ItemPosition} item from this household's plan? Say yes to remove it, or no to keep it.
It has been removed from the plan.
Nothing was removed. It stays in the plan.
CareLoop is reading today's plan back to you.
How should I say it? You can ask for it slower, louder, softer, shorter or the usual way.
Slower now.
Louder now.
Softer now.
The short version.
Back to the usual pace and length.
For this session I will answer as {Person}. What I can read out is bounded by what your household lets {Person} hear.
I don't say amounts out loud. Open the CareLoop companion page for this household to read the exact words your clinician recorded, amounts included.

If anyone is in danger right now, please call your local emergency number. In India you can call 112, or the Tele-MANAS mental-health helpline 14416 (toll-free, 24x7). I have not saved this as a care item.

stopHandling.note: Cancel and stop are supplied by the platform, so they are not restated here: the developer's copy stays free of platform brand terms.

voiceProfile.note: Whose voice the device is answering for, declared here so neither device invents a field name. The identification is SIMULATED: a browser device and a scripted driver cannot hear a voice, so the customer (or the script) states who is speaking and the device passes that statement to the server as the MCP request's own _meta. The server, not the device, decides what that member may hear, from the scope the household itself stored; an out-of-scope question is refused and the refusal is recorded. On a real deployment the same decision would be made against the verified identity behind the linked account, which is why the device's claim is labelled as a claim and the profile value names itself as simulated. Nothing on this path writes, and no dose rides it: the refusal is one of the artifact's own sentences.
